text:
Maria: heads-up — apiserver 503 spike in us-east1 starting ~09:03 UTC. controller-manager restarted twice, and etcd leader election timeouts showing up. gpu-provisioner reporting attach backlog at the same time.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-7892 (auto) — see /incidents/INC-7892

Kevin: looking now. any recent NAT or egress policy changes?

Maria: we rolled an egress/nat-policy at ~08:50. kube-proxy on edge nodes shows conntrack drops. snippet from kube-proxy: 
```
Aug 12 09:02 kube-proxy conntrack: conntrack: nf_conntrack: table full
```

Dan: conntrack table full would lead to half-open connections and fd exhaustion on LB/proxies -> apiserver 5xxs. check node-level conntrack counts: `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count` and `watch -n1 ss -s`

Lia: will bump conntrack on edge nodes now and adjust conntrack timeouts temporarily. cc @Maria

Kevin: controller-manager logs show repeated sync failures: `E112 09:03:21 controller-runtime.manager controller-runtime manager sync failed: apiserver response 503` — fanout from controllers is amplifying the effect.

Maria: gpu-provisioner metrics: attach_queue_length jumped from ~5 to ~240 around 09:05. when apiserver is slow, pods stay Pending and provisioner keeps retrying attach -> attach storm.

Dan: temporary mitigation options: drain a subset of provisioner worker nodes to reduce attach churn or pause provisioner workers for a bit to let control plane recover.

Kevin: rolling back nat-policy now (starting rollback). Lia, can you apply conntrack bump? `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288` and reduce TIME_WAIT aggressiveness?

Lia: applied to 6 edge nodes (edge-{12..17}), increased nf_conntrack_max and lowered TCP_FIN/timeout for short-lived conns. also tuned kube-proxy conntrack-based settings. monitoring metrics.

ops-bot: Deploy bot: nat-policy rollback deployed (rev 68ef2) — rollback completed at 09:17 UTC.

Maria: apiserver 5xxs trending back to normal, attach_queue dropping to ~18, controller-manager restarts stopped. keeping watch for 15m.

Kevin: follow-ups: add alerts for conntrack_utilization > 70% and attach_queue > 50, and add a short-term rate limit to provisioner attach retries. consider adding jitter/exponential backoff to prevent synchronized retries.

Dan: created INFRA-1427 on infra board: "Reduce attach retry aggressiveness & add jitter; alert on attach queue growth".

Maria: thanks all :thumbsup: leaving thread open for 30m, will escalate if it recurs.
